Berenguer de Cruïlles was a Catalan nobleman and statesman who played a crucial role in the politics of the region during the 14th century. As the bishop of Girona from 1349 to 1362, he worked to promote the interests of the Catalan Courts and to strengthen the region's position within the Kingdom of Aragon.

During his tenure as president of the Generalitat de Catalunya from 1359 to 1362, de Cruïlles implemented various reforms aimed at improving the lives of the region's citizens, including the establishment of a new system of taxation and the promotion of trade and commerce.

Despite his efforts, de Cruïlles faced significant challenges, including the threat of the Black Death and the tensions between the Catalan Courts and the Kingdom of Aragon.

Today, de Cruïlles is remembered as a key figure in the history of Catalonia, and his legacy continues to be celebrated by historians and scholars.

Berenguer de Cruïlles was born into a noble family and was educated at the University of Paris, where he studied theology and philosophy.

The legacy of Berenguer de Cruïlles can be seen in the many institutions and organizations that he helped to establish, including the Generalitat de Catalunya and the Cathedral of Barcelona.

In 2019, the city of Girona commemorated the 700th anniversary of de Cruïlles' birth with a series of events and exhibitions that celebrated his life and legacy.

As a leading figure in the Catalan Courts, de Cruïlles was known for his intelligence, his strategic thinking, and his ability to build alliances with other powerful leaders in the region.

Throughout his life, de Cruïlles remained committed to the ideals of Catalan independence and self-determination, and his legacy continues to inspire new generations of Catalan nationalists.

In 2018, the Spanish government officially recognized de Cruïlles as a national hero, and his statue was unveiled in the Cathedral of Barcelona.

Berenguer de Cruïlles (1310-1362) was the bishop of Girona from 1349 to 1362 and the first president of the Generalitat de Catalunya from 1359 to 1362, nominated by the Catalan Courts held in Cervera in 1359.

As bishop, de Cruïlles played a crucial role in the Catholic Church's efforts to suppress the spread of the Black Death in the region. He also oversaw the construction of several new churches and monasteries, including the iconic Sant Pere de Girona. His presidency of the Generalitat de Catalunya marked a significant moment in the region's struggle for autonomy and self-governance.

The legacy of Berenguer de Cruïlles can be seen in the continued development of the Generalitat de Catalunya and the enduring influence of the Catholic Church in the region. His leadership during the Black Death pandemic demonstrates the importance of effective governance and public health policies in times of crisis.

"The health of the people is the health of the state," de Cruïlles once said, highlighting the interconnectedness of public health and political leadership.
